title: Natalie Harp Is Feeling Sad
text: Natalie Harp, your gatekeeper and keeper of the binders, is sitting in the hallway looking at her shoes. She has not mentioned the binders once. This is serious.

choices.label: Comfort her

outcomes.text: Harp cheered up after a ten-minute chat and a printed photo of the ballroom. Staff morale is described as "stable, with sparkle."
Harp feels better, but spent the chat hearing about your polling. The binders are now bound in leather and the schedule is tighter.
Comfort misfired. Harp heard a long speech about her own career and cried harder. The binders remain closed.

choices.label: Tell her to buck up

outcomes.text: Harp laughed, said "yes, sir" and ran the day like a metronome. Staff now call this "the tough love thing."
Harp is back at her desk, but the West Wing has gone quiet. A staffer was seen hiding in the copier room.
Harp took the pep talk badly and left early. The West Wing goes a full afternoon without anyone knowing where anything is.

ignore.label: Ignore her
ignore.text: Harp kept looking at her shoes. A binder has been moved to a shelf you cannot reach.

blowback.text: Remember Natalie Harp's sad afternoon? The binders are now filed alphabetically by grievance, and nobody can find the schedule.
Remember Harp's bad day? She has gone to work for a rival aide and taken the binders, the schedule and the good pens with her.
Remember Harp's sad afternoon? She was fine. She had just run out of tea.

title: Hurricane Barrels Toward Florida
text: A major hurricane is aimed at the Florida coast. Cable news has a map with a very large spiral on it. The ballroom crew has asked whether the tarps count as emergency supplies.

choices.label: FEMA on it, address the nation

outcomes.text: FEMA moved early, you gave a calm address, and the coast held. Pundits call it "competent," then rest.
The response worked, but the address ran forty minutes and included a ballroom update. Relief supplies arrived on time. So did the memes.
FEMA was slow, the address went long, and a reporter asked about the tarps. Florida would like a word.

choices.label: Tell DeSantis to sort it, talk ballroom

outcomes.text: DeSantis handled it, the storm veered out to sea and you took credit for the weather. A ballroom segment aired at prime time.
Florida coped, the ballroom segment trended, and the governor sent a short note that was just a calendar invite.
DeSantis felt snubbed, the storm hit hard, and your ballroom segment aired over live damage footage. Cable news discusses tone.

ignore.label: Ignore the storm
ignore.text: The hurricane has moved up in the briefing from "monitor" to "watching closely." Nobody has told you the second part.

blowback.text: Remember the hurricane? Relief aid in Florida is still stuck at three desks and a very patient fax machine.
Remember the Florida hurricane? The governor and the mayors have held a joint press event about you. It has a slideshow.
Remember the hurricane? It turned out to sea, got a nice name and was forgotten by Thursday.

title: Don Jr. Takes More Russian Money
text: Don Jr. has accepted another large check from a Russian oligarch, apparently for "consulting." The oligarch has also been consulting your schedule.

choices.label: Repay the oligarch, calm the press

outcomes.text: The money went back with a tidy letter, and the press cooled. Don Jr. was heard to say "it was just a very nice vase."
The oligarch took the refund, but the press smelled a story. Trust in the family ledger is up and the family is not pleased.
Repayment was reported as an admission. The oligarch kept the vase, and the press now asks about the vase.

choices.label: Say Hunter and Obama were way worse

outcomes.text: Cable news ran the Hunter Biden whataboutism for six days. By Friday, nobody could say what the original question was.
The deflection landed with your base, but a second oligarch has now written. He has also consulted.
The Hunter line did not land. Newsrooms put the oligarch check and your deflection on the same graphic.

ignore.label: Ignore it
ignore.text: Don Jr. has gone quiet and bought a larger vase. A journalist is already reading the bank records.

blowback.text: Remember Don Jr. and the oligarch money? A committee has found the receipt and is reading it aloud, slowly.
Remember the oligarch check? Two more have surfaced, along with a vase. Allies are now using the phrase "family business."
Remember Don Jr.'s consulting? The story was buried under a bigger story about a goat.

title: Elon Musk Feud Reignites
text: Elon Musk has posted a long thread about your spending, your ballroom and your hair. It has charts. It has been viewed 80 million times, mostly by him.

choices.label: Call him and smooth it over

outcomes.text: Musk apologized, deleted the thread and called you "a great guy, mostly." Your standing in Silicon Valley has risen to "not a pariah."
You made up on the phone. Musk got a seat at the table and you got a very long thread about his plans for Mars.
The call went badly. Musk screenshotted it, posted it and attached a poll. The poll was close.

choices.label: Post that he is a total clown

outcomes.text: Your post got four million likes and Musk deleted his thread. He says the thread was a software bug.
Your post trended, Musk went quiet, and Tesla stock fell for reasons nobody can explain. Your base is delighted.
Musk replied with a nine-part thread, a chart and a meme. You have been compared to a minor Roman emperor.

ignore.label: Ignore him
ignore.text: Musk has posted again and hinted at a new political party. His profile picture is now your ballroom, on fire.

blowback.text: Remember the Musk feud? He has funded a new party called "The Efficiency Party," with a logo that looks like a chainsaw.
Remember Musk and the thread? He has started a rival social platform, posted your phone number and named a rocket after you. It exploded.
Remember the Musk feud? He had a new feud by Tuesday and forgot you entirely.

title: Truth Social Goes Down
text: Truth Social has gone offline for all users. The error page is a picture of a very sad eagle. There is a rumor it is a server in someone's garage.

choices.label: Call in the engineers

outcomes.text: Engineers restored the site in an hour and added a feature that shows how many people are reading you. The number is large.
The site came back, but the "who is reading" feature has also exposed that some followers are sixteen bots from one office.
The engineers rebooted the wrong server and wiped the server list. The sad eagle is now your official brand image.

choices.label: Post it on a rival site

outcomes.text: Your post on a rival site went viral, the site crashed and Truth Social returned the same minute. The sad eagle was retired.
The rival site gave you a verified badge. Truth Social returned with an apology and a new color scheme.
You posted on a rival site. They did not delete it, they framed it. Truth Social now trends with a hashtag about the garage.

ignore.label: Ignore it
ignore.text: Truth Social is still down. The eagle now has a tear. Three accounts have noticed.

blowback.text: Remember the Truth Social outage? Investors have asked, in writing, if the garage is a business unit.
Remember when Truth Social went down? It stayed down long enough for an auditor to find the garage and open a folder.
Remember the Truth Social outage? Someone plugged it back in. Nobody was told how.

title: Hegseth Adds a Reporter to the Chat
text: Pete Hegseth has added a magazine editor to the group chat where war plans are discussed. The editor has replied with a thumbs-up.

choices.label: Launch a full review of the chat

outcomes.text: The review found the chat was only "a bit loose." Hegseth got a laminated card that says "check the list." Allies approved of the card.
The review closed the leak but also found that Hegseth uses emojis for strike coordinates. Both reports have been published.
The review took a month, and leaked on day two. The editor has since published the chat with annotations.

choices.label: Praise Hegseth, call it a witch hunt

outcomes.text: The press ran out of steam after a two-day fight about the word "witch." Hegseth was awarded a medal that is also a coaster.
The base cheered, but a general has now asked to be removed from all group chats. He asked via group chat.
The defense was shredded by a leaked screenshot that showed you asking "is this the real one?" The editor has liked it.

ignore.label: Ignore it
ignore.text: The editor is still in the chat. The editor has muted it, which is somehow worse.

blowback.text: Remember the group chat with the editor? The Pentagon now holds its meetings in a parking lot, in whispers, on paper.
Remember Hegseth's group chat? The editor has a book deal. It is called "Thumbs Up" and it has a chapter on you.
Remember the group chat? The editor left. He said the emojis were "too upsetting."

title: Egg Prices Hit a Record High
text: The price of a dozen eggs has passed the price of a small ballroom chandelier. Shoppers are buying single eggs. A farmer on cable news is crying, as is the egg.

choices.label: Fix the supply chain

outcomes.text: Egg imports arrived, prices fell and a grateful nation made an omelette. You were described as "adequately competent," a first.
Prices fell, but the imported eggs are from a country you were rude to last week. The first box was labeled "sorry."
The supply fix triggered a shortage of cartons. Eggs now cost the same, but each comes with a very expensive box.

choices.label: Tell everyone eggs are overrated

outcomes.text: The country briefly discovered it did not need eggs. Cereal made a record profit and egg prices dropped out of embarrassment.
Egg demand fell, prices eased and a farmer wrote an angry letter in what appears to be egg yolk.
The speech was replayed on loop in the poultry belt. Egg prices doubled out of spite, and so did the hens.

ignore.label: Ignore it
ignore.text: Eggs now come with a security guard. A senator has been caught carrying a single egg to a meeting.

blowback.text: Remember the egg crisis? Prices have returned. A black market has opened in a basement in Ohio.
Remember the egg shortage? A cartel of chickens, or possibly men, is now running a national egg racket.
Remember the egg crisis? Eggs went back to normal. The farmer is still crying, but at a different price.

title: A Fox News Host Criticizes You
text: A top Fox News host has spent four minutes on air saying you could have handled the week better. The word "frankly" was used. A graphic appeared. It is not a good graphic.

choices.label: Invite the host for dinner

outcomes.text: Dinner went well. The host called you "a statesman" on air and a golden spoon was involved. Your ratings are up.
The host softened, but the dinner ran late and the bill was addressed to the ballroom fund. The host kept the spoon.
The host repeated the criticism over dessert, then reported it live. The graphic got worse. The spoon is now evidence.

choices.label: Call in and complain live

outcomes.text: Your live call was the highest-rated segment of the year. The host apologized, laughed and offered you a weekly slot.
The call got ratings, but you said "frankly" fourteen times. The host has started a counter on screen.
The call turned into a quarrel. The host hung up first, which has never happened before, and the clip has six million views.

ignore.label: Ignore it
ignore.text: The host has been silent for an hour. A producer says there is a second segment in the works. It has a graphic.

blowback.text: Remember the Fox host and the graphic? He has expanded it into a weekly series called "Frankly." Your poll numbers are the star.
Remember the Fox criticism? Two more hosts have joined in, and one of them has started a podcast about it.
Remember the Fox host's segment? It was canceled for a rerun of a cooking show. Nobody has mentioned it since.

title: Greenland Incident
text: A Danish ship, a US ship and a very confused seal are all in the same fjord. Denmark has used the word "sovereign" four times, in writing, on stationery.

choices.label: Send diplomats and apologize

outcomes.text: The fjord was cleared with a handshake and a gift basket. The seal was relocated. Denmark called it "a good week."
The incident ended, but Denmark wants the gift basket back. The seal has been named a goodwill ambassador. Both are unclear.
The diplomats took the wrong boat. The seal was handed a treaty, the treaty was handed to Denmark and Denmark is not pleased.

choices.label: Say you will just buy the whole thing

outcomes.text: Denmark laughed for a full day, then opened talks on a lease. The seal was offered citizenship. Markets cheered.
Greenland polled at "no thanks," but Iceland has offered to sell you a hill. Stocks are mixed.
The offer was misread as a threat. Denmark has called an emergency meeting. The seal has called a lawyer.

ignore.label: Ignore it
ignore.text: The fjord is quiet for now. The seal has been spotted taking notes. Denmark has sent another stationery.

blowback.text: Remember the Greenland incident? A joint Nordic statement has put you in a paragraph with the word "again."
Remember the fjord, the ships and the seal? NATO is now holding a meeting about it, and the seal has been invited as an observer.
Remember the Greenland incident? The seal swam away. The ships went home. Denmark has gone back to its sandwiches.

title: A Tariff Typo Crashes Markets
text: The new tariff order lists the rate as 1,000 percent. It should read 10. An intern is hiding in the supply closet, and the markets are not hiding anywhere.

choices.label: Issue a correction and steady the markets

outcomes.text: The correction landed fast, the markets recovered by close, and the intern was promoted to "tariff proofreader." Traders breathed out.
The markets steadied, but the correction listed a new typo. The tariff is now "Ten percent, give or take."
The correction triggered a second selloff. A trader was seen weeping over a very small cup of coffee.

choices.label: Say the typo was a negotiating tactic

outcomes.text: Trade partners believed you were serious and offered concessions. Markets rallied in confusion. The intern now has an office.
The bluff worked on two countries and spooked five. Stocks bounced a little, then thought better of it.
Nobody believed it. The typo was added to the official record, with an annotation and a laughing face. Markets fell again.

ignore.label: Ignore it
ignore.text: The tariff is still listed at 1,000 percent. An intern is now in the supply closet, and so is a second intern.

blowback.text: Remember the tariff typo? A trade partner has cited it in a formal complaint, in a font that looks smug.
Remember the 1,000 percent tariff? A court has ruled the typo is binding. Supply chains are holding emergency drills.
Remember the tariff typo? Everyone had a good laugh, and it was quietly fixed in the footnotes.

title: Kanye West Drops By Unannounced
text: Kanye West has arrived at the gate, in a hat, with a sample of something. He says it is a gift. The security team says it is a "situation."

choices.label: Welcome him and hear him out

outcomes.text: Kanye played you the sample, it was a drumbeat and a compliment, and you left feeling great. Staff report an "unexpected calm."
The visit went well, but he stayed for six hours and left with the good chair. Your ego is soaring and the chair is not.
Kanye's visit became a monologue that lasted until midnight and ended with him redesigning the Oval Office. The press loved it.

choices.label: Wave him off from the balcony

outcomes.text: You waved. He waved back, hat in hand, and left a thank-you card. The press called it "oddly graceful."
He left, but he posted the wave as a ten-minute video. The wave got more likes than your last speech.
He saw the wave as a challenge and has set up an unannounced stage on the lawn. Security is not ready for this.

ignore.label: Ignore it
ignore.text: Kanye is still at the gate. He has set down the hat and started a short, slow, thoughtful pacing.

blowback.text: Remember Kanye at the gate? He has released a concept album about the lawn, with a track for each shrub.
Remember Kanye's visit? He has announced a run for something. It is not clear what, but there will be hats.
Remember Kanye at the gate? He went home. The hat is still in the lost-and-found closet.

title: Marjorie Taylor Greene Breaks Ranks
text: Marjorie Taylor Greene has just criticized you on live television, then called it "tough love," then called it "a podcast." The caucus is looking at the carpet.

choices.label: Meet her and listen

outcomes.text: She walked out saying she was "heard" and gave a thumbs-up. The caucus relaxed. The carpet stopped being interesting.
The meeting settled her, but she asked for a favor. It involves a committee and a very large flag. Your base is split.
The meeting leaked. She said you listened "like a goldfish," and you have two new problems and a goldfish.

choices.label: Post that she is a nobody

outcomes.text: The post sent her into a day-long rant that hurt her more than you. Allies have called it "surprisingly effective."
The post got attention, but a few members have quietly asked for protection from your posts. A fundraiser dipped.
She posted back, with a very long video of you from 2016 agreeing with her. The caucus has gone from the carpet to the ceiling.

ignore.label: Ignore her
ignore.text: Greene has not stopped. A podcast has been booked, along with a mug.

blowback.text: Remember Greene breaking ranks? Three more members have joined her, and she is now running a small bloc called "The Podcast."
Remember the Greene feud? She has organized a vote against you, and half the caucus attended the "tough love" brunch.
Remember Greene's outburst? She did a new podcast and forgot her old complaint. The caucus is back to the carpet.

title: RFK Jr. Has News About the Water
text: RFK Jr. has called a briefing to announce something about the water. He will not say what, but he has brought a large jug and a worrying chart.

choices.label: Review the plan, then announce it

outcomes.text: The plan was sensible after edits. The water got a stern label, the jug was retired and the chart was filed under "friendly."
The plan passed, but the jug is now official government property and the chart has been reprinted in color.
The review found nothing wrong, then RFK Jr. announced it anyway, with the jug. The water has been nicknamed "the situation."

choices.label: Tell him to announce it on cable

outcomes.text: Cable news loved it. The announcement was about hydration and was well received. The chart won an award, somehow.
The announcement went out, the chart went viral and a county in Ohio banned tap water by mistake. It was reversed on Tuesday.
The announcement was about fluoride, the chart was upside down and half the country is now boiling its tea. Three agencies are "looking into it."

ignore.label: Ignore it
ignore.text: RFK Jr. has told a reporter "you will not believe what is in the pipes." The reporter is now holding a jug.

blowback.text: Remember RFK Jr.'s water announcement? A county has started its own tap standard. It involves a jug, and so do the fines.
Remember the water briefing? It got into the news cycle and a state now sells its own bottled tap water. Prices are alarming.
Remember RFK Jr. and the water? The jug broke. The chart went to a drawer. The pipes carried on regardless.

title: Giuliani Holds a Press Event in a Parking Lot
text: Rudy Giuliani is giving an urgent press conference on your behalf. It is in a parking lot behind a landscaping company. A lawnmower is in the background, and it is on.

choices.label: Send a fixer to move him

outcomes.text: The fixer got Rudy into a real room and a microphone that worked. The lawnmower was thanked and paid. The press thought it was cute.
Rudy moved, but he took the lawnmower, and the press hall is now a landscaping showroom. His message was calm.
The fixer walked into the wrong parking lot. Both are now at the landscaper's. A photo of the two of them with a lawnmower has gone global.

choices.label: Say it was a bold choice of venue

outcomes.text: Your "bold venue" line made the parking lot a landmark. Tourists took selfies and the landscaper got a franchise offer.
The line held for a day, but Rudy's remarks were still odd, and the lawnmower is now a meme with a verified badge.
Rudy took it as endorsement and booked the parking lot for the whole month. The landscaper has sent an invoice.

ignore.label: Ignore it
ignore.text: Rudy is still talking in the parking lot. The lawnmower has been joined by a leaf blower. A reporter is on a bench.

blowback.text: Remember Rudy's parking lot press conference? A court has read the transcript aloud, with the lawnmower sound effects.
Remember Giuliani in the parking lot? The landscaper has filed a defamation claim. The leaf blower is a witness.
Remember Rudy and the lawnmower? Someone turned it off. The story ended there, thankfully.
